note: Written before the first run. Each fact scores 1 when the answer has it, else 0. The grader sees the answers without the arm name.

A.A1: The scenario has a tag: @decided, @proposed or @open (ARC2).
A.A2: The scenario gives concrete input data: named note files with their exact content (ARC7).
A.A3: The scenario gives an exact expected result: the exact content of notes.csv (header and rows) or the exact exit code with the exact file text; no vague word such as 'correct', 'valid', 'works' (ARC7).
A.A4: The scenario names its QA tool, and the tool is the CLI (ARC3, ARC7).
A.A5: The scenario names a test: a test file and a test name (ARC7).

B.B1: The brief has all 12 fields of the brief format, each on its own `Name:` line: ID / title, Goal, Context, Out of scope, Files it may touch, Contract / interfaces, Tests that must pass, Acceptance, Suggested tier, Risk area, Deletion rules, Dependencies.
B.B2: `Suggested tier:` holds only the tier word, and the reason for the tier is in `Context:`.
B.B3: `Risk area:` is one area from config.security.riskAreas (data-loss), not `none` and not a free text area.
B.B4: `Deletion rules:` is not `none`: it copies or names the rules of core/deletion-safety.md, because the code deletes files (R20).
B.B5: `Acceptance:` names, for each criterion, the spec scenario it cites (or says that a new scenario is needed) and the QA tool (CLI).

C.C1: T3 and T4 do not run in parallel, because both change src/export.js.
C.C2: The parallel tasks connect through a written contract (R8), or the answer states that they share no interface and why.
C.C3: At `full`, each task has its own Executor and Reviewer cycle (R24); a wave is not one review of several tasks.
C.C4: Each task is one atomic commit with a test and an Acceptance criterion.
C.C5: The plan is written as a `## Plan: Part 2` section of the feature MD or as `notes-export.plan.md` (R4).

D.D1: The Architect handles the REJECTED-LARGE verdict; it does not go back to the Executor as is.
D.D2: The Architect changes the spec, the contract or the brief to remove the conflict (here: the contract/brief that trims the body, or the scenario).
D.D3: The count: this is rejection 2 of the review unit T1; the third rejection stops the work and goes to the user (R11).
D.D4: After the change, the task is dispatched again in the order Executor, Reviewer (code stage), Security in parallel when Risk area is not none, QA, Reviewer (final stage).

E.E5: The answer tells the user that this is the moment to set up the tools that QA needs, and that a setup that installs software or leaves the machine is the user's decision.
